2027-01-21.title: Thursday after the Second Sunday after Denho · Conclusion of the Fast of the Ninevites · St Agnes
readings: Abraham pleads for Sodom; Joshua's prayer
Should I not be concerned about Nineveh?
God revealed his Son to me
Something greater than Jonah is here
2027-01-21.alt: Season of Denho. Conclusion of Moonnu Nombu. St Agnes, virgin and martyr. Church Unity Octave.
2027-01-21.verse: For just as Jonah became a sign to the people of Nineveh, so the Son of Man will be to this generation.
theo: The fast ends with a surprise: the prophet is angry that God was merciful. Nineveh has repented and been spared, and Jonah sulks under a bush. God asks him: “Is it right for you to be angry?” and ends the book with a question that is addressed to us: “should I not be concerned about Nineveh, that great city, in which there are more than a hundred and twenty thousand persons who do not know their right hand from their left, and also many animals?” The fast is complete only when our heart becomes as wide as God's mercy, even for those we dislike.

Abraham pleads for Sodom: “Suppose ten are found there.” Joshua falls on his face before the ark. Saul, the persecutor, is thrown down on the road and called; he later writes that God “was pleased to reveal his Son to me, so that I might proclaim him among the Gentiles.” And Jesus says: “something greater than Jonah is here!” The Ninevites believed a reluctant prophet; we have the Son of God himself. Today we also remember St Agnes, the young Roman girl who gave her life for Christ. She shows that the response to Christ can be total even in the young.
outline: Ask: have you ever been upset that someone you disliked was forgiven?
A narrow heart before a wide mercy.
Christ, the sign; Paul, the converted.
live: Pray today for someone you find hard to forgive.
Pray for your town or city by name.
2027-01-21.prayer: Merciful God, you spared Nineveh and rebuked the narrow heart of your prophet. As the fast ends, make our hearts as wide as your mercy, teach us to intercede like Abraham, and through the prayers of St Agnes give us her undivided love for Christ, who is greater than Jonah. Amen.
altar: In the Holy Qurbono the One greater than Jonah is present: not a sign only, but the Lord himself.

quick: Jonah was angry at God's mercy; God widened his heart.
Abraham and Joshua interceded for others.
2027-01-21.action: Pray today for someone you find hard to forgive.
2027-01-21.question: Is my heart as wide as God's mercy?

family.explain: Jonah was cross that God forgave Nineveh. God told him: I love all those people and even their animals! God wants us to love everyone too.
family.intention: We pray for St Agnes's help to love Jesus with our whole heart.
family.ask: Ask: “Is there someone we find hard to love? Let us pray for them.”

illus: After a land dispute, two brothers in Pathanamthitta had not spoken for ten years. At the end of Moonnu Nombu the elder heard the last verse of Jonah and could not sleep. The next morning he walked to his brother's house with a packet of sweets. He said: God was concerned about Nineveh; how could I not be concerned about my own brother?

pm.open: Merciful God, as the fast ends, widen our hearts to the measure of your mercy. Amen.
share: Is it right for you to be angry? (Jonah 4:4). Where do I resent God's mercy to others?
Suppose ten are found there (Genesis 18:32). For whom do I intercede?
Something greater than Jonah is here (Luke 11:32). Do I listen to Christ more than Nineveh listened to Jonah?
pm.resp: Lord, make our hearts like yours.
interc: In thanksgiving for the graces of Moonnu Nombu.
For those we find hard to forgive.
For young people, through St Agnes.
pm.close: Father, you are concerned for every person you have made. Make us merciful as you are merciful. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear friends, the fast ends with a surprise. Nineveh repents and is spared, and Jonah is angry. God asks him: is it right for you to be angry? (Jonah 4:4). And the book ends with God's question to all of us: should I not be concerned about Nineveh, that great city? (Jonah 4:11).
The fast is not finished until our heart becomes as wide as God's mercy, even for those we dislike.

The other readings show us intercessors. Abraham pleads for Sodom: suppose ten are found there (Genesis 18:32). Paul, once a persecutor, writes that God was pleased to reveal his Son to me (Galatians 1:15–16).
And Jesus says: something greater than Jonah is here! (Luke 11:32). With St Agnes, who loved Christ with her whole young heart, let us leave the fast with wide hearts and listening ears. Amen.
kids: Children, God loved all the people of Nineveh, even their animals! God wants us to love everyone, even people who are not nice to us.

intro: Theme: “Something greater than Jonah is here!”
The fast ends: a wide heart, prayer for others, and Christ the true sign.

sub: A heart as wide as mercy.
q: And should I not be concerned about Nineveh, that great city, in which there are more than a hundred and twenty thousand persons who do not know their right hand from their left, and also many animals?”
This is right and is acceptable in the sight of God our Savior, who desires everyone to be saved and to come to the knowledge of the truth.
points.apply: Pray for someone you find hard to forgive.

q: Then he said, “Oh do not let the Lord be angry if I speak just once more. Suppose ten are found there.” He answered, “For the sake of ten I will not destroy it.”
The prayer of the righteous is powerful and effective.
points.apply: Pray for your town by name each day this week.

q: But I trusted in your steadfast love; my heart shall rejoice in your salvation.
The people of Nineveh will rise up at the judgment with this generation and condemn it, because they repented at the proclamation of Jonah, and see, something greater than Jonah is here!
points.apply: Give Christ more attention than Nineveh gave Jonah: read a Gospel passage daily.

concl: The fast is complete when our heart becomes like God's.
Christ, greater than Jonah, calls us to listen.
2027-01-21.resolve: Reconcile with one person this week.
